title: Ten Sultans: AI-assisted Godot development and keeping campaign gates consistent
author: developerbb
selftext:
I'm the developer of Ten Sultans: Ottoman Chronicle / On Padişah, a released Godot mobile idle strategy game. This is a promotion of my own game, with a concrete progression-design question for other AI-assisted developers.



AI was used extensively for code/debugging and writing/localization; the miniature-style illustrations and music are AI-generated. Those are separate parts of the project: the generated illustrations present each reign, while the code has to keep the campaign, economy and succession rules consistent. English and Turkish are supported.



One concrete example is campaign readiness. Total army power, named troop requirements and sustained city income all have to pass. In the Constantinople screen, power and income are sufficient while artillery and janissaries are still below their targets. A single 'enough power' check would miss that distinction. After a succession, the realm starts again while permanent dynasty talents remain, so checking only a late-game save would miss another important state.



For AI-assisted progression code, these are useful acceptance cases to spell out explicitly: enough power with the wrong troop mix; enough troops without the required income; and the first campaign after a succession. These are checks suggested by the game's rules, not a claim about an automated test suite. How do you keep such rules aligned between generated logic and the explanation shown to players?



The released game follows ten rulers from Osman Gazi to Suleiman, with 49 campaigns, 33 troop types and 60 buildings. Free to play with optional rewarded ads and no in-app purchases.
